claim: D-435 only aborts sessions whose NaruServe sender write has been in flight for more than 1 s, but TinyHttpd's stop path can still block the stopping thread for up to the 30 s write timeout per session. Three cases are not covered: (a) the read loop's own Ping (sent after an idle interval) or Pong reply is stalled on a full send buffer while holding writeLock, and NaruServe cannot see that write; (b) a sender write started less than 1 s before the participant ran; (c) no write is in flight but the peer's receive window is full, so the 1001 close frame that fireStop writes on the stopping thread blocks. HttpServer.stop calls onServerStopping -> Upgraded.fireStop -> WebSocket.close(1001) one connection at a time, before its grace loop starts, so each stalled session can add up to writeTimeout. That breaks the timeout-plus-1.5 s margin of D-344 and makes T44 with stalled clients flaky.

claim: D-425 closes idle sessions from NaruServe's single scheduler thread. WebSocket.close takes writeLock and writes a frame, so a session whose socket is stalled (for example on a TinyHttpd read-loop Ping into a full buffer) blocks that thread for up to the 30 s write timeout. While it is blocked, every other session's idle timeout is late, which works against the isolation that D-320 asks for on the send side.

TinyHttpd caps each header line at inputBufferBytes - 2, not only the request line. D-414 sizes inputBufferBytes from the request-line limit alone. If the header-size configuration of D-225 is raised, a single header line longer than 8190 bytes (a large Cookie) still gets 431, even though the configured header size allows it.

D-426 says shutdown during STARTING waits up to its timeout for listen() to end. It does not say what shutdown returns or reports, or which state is visible, when the timeout passes while onStart is still blocked. It also does not say whether the path goes through FAILED before TERMINATED, which D-427 and the object.md §11.3 diagram (STARTING -fail-> FAILED -> TERMINATED) distinguish.
